# Pinned downloads (security row 16): every binary or archive CI fetches by URL.
#
# One line per asset: `<sha256>  <url>`. scripts/fetch-pinned.sh reads this file,
# refuses a URL that is not listed here, and aborts the step when the bytes it
# got (downloaded, or restored from actions/cache) hash to anything else.
# scripts/check-action-pins.sh refuses a CI download that bypasses it.
#
# Bumping a version = add the new line (digest from the exact release asset:
# `curl -fsSL -o f <url> && shasum -a 256 f`) in the same commit that changes
# the version, and drop the old line once nothing names it.

# Third-party actions (each pinned to a commit by check-action-pins.sh) and what
# each FETCHES when it runs — the part a commit pin cannot freeze. The gate
# refuses an action that is not declared here, so a new one lands saying it.
#   action <owner/repo> <what it fetches at run time>
action actions/checkout  this repository's own git objects (an acceptance-ring project only at a 40-hex `ref:`, gated); no executable
action actions/cache  cache entries this repository's own runs saved; no executable from outside the repository
action actions/upload-artifact  nothing (uploads)
action actions/download-artifact  artifacts this run's own jobs uploaded; no executable from outside the run
action Swatinem/rust-cache  cache entries this repository's own runs saved; no executable from outside the repository
action dtolnay/rust-toolchain  runs the runner's rustup for an exact toolchain (gated by action_supply `versions`); rustup checks every component against the sha256 in that release's channel manifest from static.rust-lang.org — bounded by the Rust release infrastructure, not by a digest stated here
action actions/attest-build-provenance  no executable; signs through Sigstore (Fulcio / Rekor) and the GitHub attestations API
